content: 1. Childhood vaccinations should ideally be administered prior to initiating myeloablative conditioning procedures. 2. Antiretroviral (ART) medications, such as nelfinavir, nevirapine, raltegravir, rilpivirine, ritonavir, tipranavir, tenofovir DF, and zidovudine, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. These medications should be avoided or replaced with alternatives. ARTs must not be taken for at least one month before cell mobilization or for the expected duration required for their elimination. 3. The safety and effectiveness of vaccinations, including pneumococcal vaccines (13-valent, 15-valent, 20-valent, 21-valent, and polyvalent), poliovirus vaccine (inactivated), rabies vaccine (including chick embryo cell-derived), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines (adjuvanted and mRNA), rotavirus oral vaccine (live), smallpox and monkeypox vaccines (live, non-replicating), typhoid vaccines (polysaccharide and live), varicella virus vaccine (live), yellow fever vaccine, and zoster vaccines (live and recombinant), during or following atidarsagene autotemcel treatment have not been studied. 4. Vaccination is not recommended during the six weeks preceding the start of myeloablative conditioning and until hematologic recovery is achieved following treatment. 5. If feasible, childhood vaccinations should be completed before initiating myeloablative conditioning. 6. Atidarsagene autotemcel must not be administered during pregnancy due to risks associated with myeloablative conditioning. A negative serum pregnancy test must be confirmed before starting mobilization, reconfirmed before conditioning procedures, and before administration in females of childbearing potential. 7. There are no clinical data on the presence of atidarsagene autotemcel in human or animal milk, its effects on breastfed children, or its impact on milk production. Breastfeeding should be discontinued during myeloablative conditioning due to potential risks. 8. Breastfeeding after infusion should be discussed with the treating physician. Children receiving breast milk may continue to do so during treatment under the advice of their treating physician. 9. Controlled studies in pregnant women have not been conducted to assess the potential for fetal harm when atidarsagene autotemcel is administered. Animal reproductive and developmental toxicity studies have also not been performed. 10. The decision to breastfeed after treatment should be made in consultation with the treating physician, considering the potential risks associated with myeloablative conditioning.
